title: Uffici companion fixture script, v1
description: The scripted agents host's format. It is the ONE scripted-host format in the product: the smoke's fixture plugin plays the same file, in another language, which is why the structure is described here rather than only in the companion's Go validator. Cross-references a schema cannot express — a cause entry naming an entry that exists, a through cursor inside the conversation — are checked at load by the companion.

logs.description: What the scripted host answers a logs ticket with (#2267). Absent: shipping on, the harness at warn — the platform's default. The CI script raises the harness to info so a turn's Hermes lines are shipped and the e2e can assert all three sources.

tools.description: The AGENT's tool catalog, as the platform lists it (the wire's tools.list result), served for every conversation: on the platform the catalog is the agent's, the same in each conversation it works in. Absent: the agent has no tools.

results.description: Each tool's scripted answer, by tool name, given verbatim to every call of it, in any conversation: the result, and the callUrn that names the call (absent: null, a call that did not run). A listed tool with no answer answers {"ok": true} and a null callUrn; an answer for a tool the catalog does not list is refused at load.

memory.description: The agent's memory (#2385). Absent: a working memory — what a request remembers in a conversation is recalled there, newest first, by a query sharing one of its words of four or more letters (a stand-in for the platform's search: the e2e asserts the round trip, not the ranking). `unavailable: true` answers every memory op `platform_unavailable`, the knowledge-api-down case.

unavailableIn.description: The conversations, by name, whose memory ops answer `platform_unavailable`: memory working in one conversation of a run and down in another.

offset.description: The companion's agent's committed position, the exclusive lower bound of the next delta. Advances only on an answered or empty close. EMPTY is legitimate and means nothing has been read yet, so the first delta covers the whole transcript.

context.description: What the scripted host answers with this conversation's delta read: the platform's composed context, as the brief carries it (the wire's context.schema.json). Absent: the read carries none, as from an older gateway.

self.description: True for the companion's OWN agent. Its entries are excluded from a delta and included in an opener.

note.description: Free prose for the reader, ignored by the runner. A script is a description of a scenario, and the reason a step expects what it expects is often the most useful thing in the file — JSON has no comments, so this is where it goes.

assertions.description: The terminal tally. Counts, never a transcript — and ringsDelivered has a floor, because a run that asserted only 'nothing failed' would pass over a script whose steps never fired.

ringsDelivered.description: 🔴 The FLOOR (at least one) is the companion's check, not this schema's: the split is that the schema says what shape a script has and the loader says what it MEANS. Present and an integer is the shape; 'a script that asserts nothing is not a script' is the meaning, and the loader's refusal says so in words.

toolCalls.description: When present, exactly how many tool calls reached the scripted host — zero included.

memoryOps.description: How many of each memory op reached the scripted host, for the ops named; an op not named is not asserted.

note.description: Free prose for the reader, ignored by the runner. Why a tally is what it is — a count that looks wrong until somebody explains it costs the next reader an hour.
